title: Therapy-Based Extension Months on a Patient Payment Plan Modification
content:
**Training questions — therapy and the extension months of a Patient Payment Plan modification**

**How does a patient's therapy bear on a modification?**
The treatment months follow the patient's therapy on their Insured Plans of Care: with at least 4 visits billed within the last 2 months on any of the patient's plans of care and no patient statement issued on any of them within the last 6 months, they are 2; with at least one but fewer than 4 such visits and no such statement, they are 1; otherwise they are zero. The treatment months are added to the extension months of the modification, which are never more than the tier's maximum term extension in total.

**Which records are read?**
The billed-visit entries and the issued patient-statement entries on every Insured Plan of Care the patient holds, each placed by the date it was recorded. An entry lies within the last N months when fewer than N whole calendar months separate its date from the handling date.

**Does a recent statement matter even with many visits?**
Yes. A patient statement issued on any of the patient's plans of care within the last 6 months gives zero treatment months, however many visits were billed.

## Table

| Visits billed within the last 2 months (all of the patient's Insured Plans of Care) | Statement issued within the last 6 months | Treatment months |
|---|---|---|
| 4 or more | No | 2 |
| 1 to 3 | No | 1 |
| 0 | No | 0 |
| Any number | Yes | 0 |

## Hypothetical cases

- Six visits billed in the last 2 months across two Insured Plans of Care, last statement 9 months ago: 2 treatment months.
- Exactly 4 visits, no statement in 6 months: 2. Exactly 3 visits: 1.
- Five visits, and a statement issued 4 months ago on one of the plans of care: 0.
